evidence: M-O s.v. Virgin Mary: Deipara Virgō (Tursellinus, 1652)
terms.comment: “She who bore God”, Latin for Greek Θεοτόκος, the title confirmed at Ephesus (431) and used in both churches.

evidence: Cod. Just. 1.1.6: theotocos virgō Marīa (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The Greek title itself, in Latin letters.
The usual name in the Latin liturgy; genetrīx, mother, is classical (Enn., Verg.; Lewis & Short). Its early attestation was not checked here.

phrases.latin: Et unde hoc mihi, ut veniat māter Dominī meī ad mē?
phrases.english: And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?

sources: Lewis & Short: deipara · Lewis & Short: theotocos · Lewis & Short: genetrix
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Virgin Mary.
